questions.q: What does Roth say our reasons really are?
a: Excuses that keep us from changing our behavior
Honest explanations we should accept
Signs that the goal was poorly chosen
Lessons we can apply next time
questions.why: Lesson 1 argues reasons block decisions and real change.

questions.q: What does the summary say about the causes we assign to events?
a: They are often correlations rather than real causes
They reveal patterns we can reliably predict
They are usually more accurate than we assume
They matter less than the events themselves
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses the spilled coffee and phone call examples to show false links.

questions.q: What is the point of saying and instead of but?
a: It nudges your mind to find a way to do both
It makes your speech sound more positive
It helps you avoid committing to anything
It softens bad news when talking to others
questions.why: Lesson 2 says reframing turns a sacrifice into a solvable problem.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest treating people you meet?
a: As potential friends you genuinely want to help
As contacts who may prove useful later
As equals to negotiate with carefully
As audiences for your expertise
questions.why: Lesson 3 says networking fails when you treat people as business contacts.

questions.q: What happens when you share ideas and knowledge freely?
a: It tends to return to you many times over
People start expecting free help from you
You lose the advantage of exclusive knowledge
It only pays off inside your own company
questions.why: Lesson 3 argues an abundance mindset multiplies what you give away.
